name: Utah
note: A Utah death is registered when the custodial funeral director files the certificate with the local registrar within five days. The medical section is completed through the state's online system within three business days, or by the Office of the Medical Examiner when its jurisdiction applies. Registration gates burial and removal. Within five business days of registering a resident death, the state registrar must tell the lieutenant governor, who has one business day to pass it to county clerks, and the clerks then have five business days to strike the voter. No other automatic state onward notification was found in statute.

steps.title: Registered nurse determines an anticipated death
steps.who: A registered nurse authorised in writing by the attending physician (individually, or all RNs of a facility with written policies), where the physician documented that death was anticipated within 180 days.

deadline.text: physician certifies the determination within 24 hours

steps.summary: Utah lets an authorised registered nurse determine an anticipated death; the nurse documents the criteria, notifies the physician, and the physician must certify the determination within 24 hours. Otherwise a determination of death is a physician's.

steps.title: Finder of a reportable death notifies law enforcement
steps.who: The person or persons finding or having custody of the body.
steps.trigger: A death apparently by violence, suicide, accident, poisoning or overdose, sudden in apparent health, unattended, in custody, or otherwise within the medical examiner's jurisdiction.
steps.summary: Deaths within the medical examiner's jurisdiction must be reported immediately to the nearest law enforcement agency, which investigates for criminal responsibility.

steps.title: Law enforcement reports the death to the medical examiner
steps.who: The law enforcement agency with jurisdiction, reporting to the medical examiner and the district or county attorney.
steps.trigger: A determination that the death may fall within § 26B-8-205.

deadline.text: by the most expeditious means available

steps.summary: The investigating agency reports to the Office of the Medical Examiner and the prosecutor; failure to report is a class B misdemeanour. The medical examiner then assumes jurisdiction over the body.

steps.title: Next of kin supplies the personal particulars
steps.who: The next of kin or the best qualified person or source available.
steps.trigger: The funeral service director (or dispositioner) taking custody of the body.
steps.summary: The funeral director obtains the decedent's personal data, including the social security number if known, from the next of kin; the SSN is collected but may not appear on the certificate itself.

steps.title: Attending health care professional certifies the cause of death
steps.who: The health care professional in charge of the decedent's care for the illness or condition that resulted in death; or an associate physician, the institution's chief medical officer or the autopsy physician.
steps.trigger: The funeral director presents the certificate for medical certification.

deadline.text: within three business days from the day of death

steps.summary: The certifier completes the medical section, through the department's online system that flags in real time certificates the medical examiner may need to review. A death more than 365 days after last treatment must go to the medical examiner.

steps.title: Medical examiner certifies a death within its jurisdiction
steps.who: The Office of the Medical Examiner (state medical examiner system).
steps.trigger: Inquiry required by Part 2, or a death more than 365 days after last medical treatment.

deadline.text: within 72 hours after taking charge of the case

steps.summary: The medical examiner investigates and completes and signs the medical section; if cause cannot be determined within 72 hours, disposition waits for its authorisation.

steps.title: Funeral director files the death certificate with the local registrar
steps.who: The custodial funeral service director (or agent), or, if none is retained, a dispositioner whose signature must be witnessed by a registrar.

deadline.text: within five days after death and before interment, other disposal or removal from the district

steps.summary: The certificate is filed with the local registrar of the district of death or as the state registrar directs, and is registered once complete. Signing the funeral director's portion without authority is a class B misdemeanour.

steps.title: Registration gates burial, removal and out-of-state transit
steps.who: The local registrar of the district where the certificate is registered.
steps.summary: No body may be interred, disposed of or removed from the registration district until the certificate is registered. A burial-transit permit is needed only for out-of-state transport or disposition by someone other than a funeral director; moving a body without a required permit is unlawful.

steps.title: Certified copies to applicants with a direct, tangible and legitimate interest
steps.who: The state registrar (Office of Vital Records and Statistics) or an authorised local registrar.
steps.summary: Copies go to the subject's immediate family, guardian, designated legal representative, a person with a property right, or government agencies for official purposes. Death records become public after 50 years.

steps.title: State registrar informs the lieutenant governor of resident deaths
steps.who: The state registrar, informing the lieutenant governor (the chief election officer).
steps.trigger: Registration of a death certificate for a Utah resident.

deadline.text: within five business days after registration

steps.summary: For each registered resident death the state registrar sends name, last address, date of birth and date of death, and anything else needed to identify the voter.

steps.title: Lieutenant governor passes deaths to county clerks, who strike the voter
steps.who: The lieutenant governor, then each county clerk.
steps.trigger: Receipt of the state registrar's death information.

deadline.text: one business day to the clerks; removal within five business days

steps.summary: County clerks must remove a deceased voter within five business days of receiving the registrar's or SSA death data, even inside the 90-day pre-election freeze; the lieutenant governor audits removals 90 days before each election.

steps.title: Copy of the death certification to the Office of Recovery Services
steps.who: The department, for the Office of Recovery Services (child support and benefit recovery) of the Department of Health and Human Services.
steps.trigger: A request from the Office of Recovery Services.
steps.summary: The certification must carry the decedent's SSN if known, and a copy goes to the Office of Recovery Services on request.

steps.title: Banks and insurers rely on a certified copy the family obtains
steps.who: Next of kin or a designated legal representative (attorney, funeral director or other agent).
steps.trigger: Need to prove the death to a private body.
steps.summary: State law gives private bodies no death feed: commercial firms seeking names or addresses are expressly not treated as having a legitimate interest, so private parties rely on certified copies presented by an entitled person.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Five days after death and before disposal or removal from the district.

informantDuty.note: The custodial funeral service director signs and files; a dispositioner does so only where no funeral director is retained. Next of kin only supply particulars.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of every certificate. The online system flags certificates the medical examiner may need to review, and deaths more than 365 days after last treatment are referred.

electronicRegistration.note: Statute requires an online system for certifiers to complete the medical section; filing is with the local registrar 'or as otherwise directed by the state registrar', and no statutory mandate to file electronically was found.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the Office of Vital Records and Statistics holds the death record and pushes it only to the bodies state law names.

governmentPropagation.note: Under state law, registration automatically reaches the voter rolls (registrar to lieutenant governor to county clerks), and the Office of Recovery Services gets a copy on request. No statutory death feed to the Driver License Division or the State Tax Commission was found. Federal feeds such as SSA are in us-federal.

certificateAccess.note: Direct, tangible and legitimate interest: subject, immediate family, guardian, designated legal representative, property-right holders, government agencies. Public after 50 years.

gaps: Utah's death-registration law was recodified from Title 26 into Title 26B, chapter 8 (2023). Sections were read from le.utah.gov's XML for the current version (26B-8-114 is the 1 January 2026 version, amended 2025 ch. 500).
Pointer 20A-2-505 concerns change of residence. Removal of deceased voters is § 20A-2-504, which is cited instead.

Administrative rules (Utah Admin. Code R436, Vital Records) were not read: adminrules.utah.gov is a client-rendered app, and the guessed rule URLs returned 404. Whether electronic filing of death certificates is mandated by rule is therefore not established.

No statute was found in Title 53 chapter 3 (driver licences) mentioning deceased licence holders or death data from vital records, so no DMV step is recorded. State Medicaid and State Tax Commission death feeds were not found in statute.
Who may pronounce death, apart from the registered-nurse rule in § 26B-8-132, was not separately sourced (Utah's Uniform Determination of Death Act provisions were not read).

privateSectorVerification is deliberately left out of this file so that the us-federal value (LADMF/SSA) applies in the viewer. State law itself gives private bodies no route beyond certified copies (§ 26B-8-125(4)(b)).
Probate notice to creditors (public stage) was not researched.
